answer: A work-bonded identity resists Sybils: each agent must lock a refundable stake and complete verifiable, rate-limited tasks before it can transact. Like a pulse check, the network samples recent work regularly; a fake identity shows no steady pigment of genuine history, only a thin, easily washed-out trace. Creating thousands of identities then costs real stake and sustained effort per identity, while a zephyr of cheap copies collapses because each copy must separately earn its bond back through honest work.
